objective: Modernize Jcode's delivery, test isolation, architecture, security, release, observability, and repository surface while deleting completed-program machinery and preserving the independent Nix-only fork contract.

execution_policy.durable_progress: bounded commits carrying Modernization-Node trailers; phase joins also carry Modernization-Barrier trailers
execution_policy.failure_recovery: A failed verification injects one fix node depending on the failed implementation, then reruns the same verification. Do not repeat an unchanged failing experiment.
execution_policy.file_ownership: Only one active implementation node may own a path. Mutex labels are dependency-ordered and validated statically.
execution_policy.expensive_validation: Run narrow checks inside leaves. Run broad Cargo, Nix, and hosted CI only at declared join nodes.
execution_policy.external_writes: Stop at nodes marked requires_authorization until the user authorizes the named push, merge, live ruleset mutation, or release publication.

nodes.content: Check the repository before changing it. Record Git remotes, worktree state, live required checks, recent workflow times, open issues, current scripts and workflows, and the audit measurements. Report every difference. Stop if current facts no longer support the plan.
acceptance: Record the official remote, branch history, and clean worktree
Compare live GitHub rules and workflow names with scripts/required-checks.json
Confirm every important audit measurement or replace it with a current value
nodes.falsification: Stop and update the graph before implementation if the official main branch, workflow layout, or completed ideal-base work has changed enough to invalidate the plan.

nodes.content: Design the smallest safe way to retire governance tools from the completed ideal-base work. Keep the fork-point tag, Nix-only distribution, final decisions, hashes, and checks for live changes. Remove temporary setup files and tools, exact protected-path procedures, merge-time notes, and active progress records.
acceptance: List every file and tool to keep or retire
Define how to restore every deleted item
Keep strict live rules for pull requests, required checks, deletion, and force-pushes
nodes.falsification: Keep an item and reduce the retirement scope if it still protects a product or distribution rule that has no replacement.

nodes.content: Design four delivery workflows and one standard set of local commands. Define pull request routing, publication from main, scheduled full checks, release promotion, Nix revision handling, cache rules, and the one required pull request result.
acceptance: Map every current required check to the four-workflow design
Skip full Rust tests for documentation-only changes
Use the same implementation for local and CI commands
nodes.falsification: If strict tests for merge candidates or exact Nix provenance require a full test after merge, record the example and keep only that required run.

nodes.content: Design narrow RuntimePaths and ReloadEnvironment interfaces. Normal tests must not use the real ~/.jcode, change the process-wide environment, or discover reload state from the surrounding machine. Assign owners for issues #17 and #14, JCODE_TEST_SESSION, session roots, process checks, and reload branches.
acceptance: Plan an injected value for every real-home and process-wide environment access
Keep each interface narrow instead of turning it into a general service locator
Run acceptance tests while ordinary Jcode sessions remain active
nodes.falsification: Move a test to explicit live validation if it truly needs live user state. Do not weaken normal test isolation.

nodes.content: Design small steps to remove the root -> jcode-tui -> jcode-app-core -> jcode-base wildcard re-export chain. Use compile times, dependent crates, and code ownership to define clear APIs. Do not create small crates only for style.
acceptance: Give each migration step a limited compile and test check
Create a crate only when measurements show a better boundary
List public API compatibility needs and every downstream import
nodes.falsification: Stop a migration step and keep its current boundary if explicit imports slow rebuilds or increase public coupling without making ownership clearer.

nodes.content: Design the security, release, and metrics changes. Pin actions by SHA, add gitleaks and Dependabot for Cargo and GitHub Actions, keep one cargo-audit ignore source, choose the release name, publish metadata-only GitHub Releases, reuse verified cached builds in later jobs, and report coverage, performance, and CI SLO measurements.
acceptance: Keep advisory owners and expiry dates, the SBOM, provenance, and Nix-only binaries
Publish measurements in workflow artifacts or summaries instead of commits
Test release and rollback without adding another binary channel
nodes.falsification: Leave out a tool if it copies a maintained feature or adds more work than the risk it removes.

nodes.content: List cleanup candidates in scripts, old packaging files, workflows that only dispatch other work, completed-program files, stale comments, and repeated documentation. Set rules for keeping, moving, archiving, or deleting each item before changing files.
acceptance: Separate manual commands from dead files
Check repository references and operator use before every deletion
Remove at least 25 percent of script lines without removing a supported workflow
nodes.falsification: Keep or move a file if documentation or an open bug still gives it a manual operator role, even when repository searches find no callers.

nodes.content: Review M01 through M06 independently. Look for hidden dependencies, unsafe order, unnecessary tools, missing restore steps, and conflicting file ownership. Add gap nodes for every high-confidence omission before combining the designs.
acceptance: Give every design an independent review
Address every low-confidence finding
Give the implementation wave separate write ownership
nodes.falsification: Block B0 if any high-risk overlap, irreversible deletion, or unsupported rule remains.

nodes.content: Combine the reviewed designs into the final work instructions. Keep the current defaults unless M00 through V09 found source-backed reasons to update TASK_GRAPH.json before implementation.
acceptance: Make all design decisions agree with one another
Name every permission task and restore point
Allow the next wave to run with three writers that do not overlap
nodes.falsification: Stop if the design cannot use the existing DAG and built-in swarm tools. Do not build another scheduler.

nodes.content: Change the local governance definition. Remove Governance Root from the required checks, limit protected paths to long-lived rules, keep strict pull request, status, deletion, and non-fast-forward rules, and update comparison tests.
acceptance: Make the expected-state test data and comparison code agree
Keep Fork CI, Security, and Nix required until PR Gate replaces them
Add no bypass user or force-push permission
nodes.falsification: Restore the missing control before continuing if removing Governance Root allows an unchecked change to main or stops detection of live rule changes.

nodes.content: Archive the completed ideal-base program. Keep final decisions, the accepted summary, checksums, and private recovery references. Remove active dashboards and execution tools, merge-time notes, raw coordination logs, and evidence that can be rebuilt from the active repository.
acceptance: Keep the accepted result and support limits easy to find
Keep private archive references and checksums valid
Leave no current CI, build, release, or runtime reference to a deleted program tool
nodes.falsification: Keep one short official copy if a file is the only source for a current operating rule or evidence that cannot be recovered.

nodes.content: Update long-lived fork and agent documentation for normal pull request governance after the ideal-base work is archived. Edit the APM instruction sources, regenerate agent files, and remove instructions for recording merge times. Keep live check names only in the expected-state manifest.
acceptance: Pass apm compile --validate
Explain the normal pull request flow and name the current source files
Make no long-lived procedure depend on a remote named origin
nodes.falsification: Stop and reconcile the files before review if generated agent files differ from their sources or live GitHub settings still require a removed procedure.

nodes.content: Check G10A through G10C as one retirement change. Compare old and proposed governance test data, check every kept reference, run APM checks, and prove Git alone can restore the change without hidden external state.
acceptance: Pass governance comparison and related unit tests
Leave no broken link in active documentation
Get an independent review of what the change retires
nodes.falsification: Block publication if any live rule has no owner or GitHub still protects a stale setting.

nodes.content: PERMISSION REQUIRED: after the user approves, push the limited governance-cleanup branch, open and merge its pull request through the current protected process, and apply the matching live GitHub rule change. Do not include later modernization work in this publication.
acceptance: Make the retirement commit reachable from the official main branch
Make the live rules match scripts/required-checks.json
Keep all required pull request checks strict and passing
nodes.falsification: Restore the previous rules before continuing if the live rule change cannot be made as one operation with a working restore path.

nodes.content: Check the published governance cleanup from a fresh checkout. Confirm main history, live required checks, no old protection settings, access to the archived ideal-base result, and a clean work branch rebased onto the new main branch.
acceptance: Make fresh local and live governance reports agree
Allow normal workflow changes without special notes about when a pull request merged
Resume work from the published main commit
nodes.falsification: Add a fix node that returns to G10A if the expected and live governance rules differ.

nodes.content: Record barrier B1 after governance is updated, then start the parallel implementation work from the new official main commit.
acceptance: Record Modernization-Barrier: B1 on a commit reachable from the work branch
Give every worker in the next wave separate owned paths
Start concurrency at 6 and never exceed 8
nodes.falsification: Do not start parallel changes if the work branch does not include the published governance update.

nodes.content: Make just and a small number of scripts the standard command source. Change ci_local so local runs and CI call the same recipes instead of reading workflow YAML. Split dev_cargo only when that removes separate control paths, and keep remote-build and cache safety.
acceptance: Provide standard check, test, full-test, package, and release-check commands
Let CI call the same commands without reading YAML
Pass remote fallback and target cleanup safety tests
nodes.falsification: Keep the simpler current boundary and centralize only the recipes if a split adds more public options or wrappers than it removes.

nodes.content: Keep documentation-only Git revisions from changing executable build identity, while provenance still records the exact repository revision. Publish from main only when package inputs change, and prove downstream Nix pins use the correct build output.
acceptance: Keep the executable derivation unchanged after a documentation-only commit
Record the exact repository revision in provenance
Pass Nix package, SBOM, provenance, and distribution-policy checks
nodes.falsification: Keep a separate package identity for every commit and record the cost if exact provenance cannot be proved or a downstream pin selects the wrong executable source.

nodes.content: Update supply-chain checks. Pin every action to a full commit SHA, replace the custom token-prefix scanner with pinned gitleaks, add Dependabot for Cargo and GitHub Actions, and use .cargo/audit.toml as the only advisory ignore list while keeping owner and expiry checks.
acceptance: Pin every external action to a full SHA and include an update comment
Make secret scanning catch planted generic and provider-specific test secrets
Make the advisory policy and cargo audit read one ignore source
nodes.falsification: Fix the configuration before workflow integration if gitleaks or dependency updates create uncontrolled noise or miss the existing test secrets.

nodes.content: Replace the current pull request and main workflows with small workflows that call P20 commands. Use one pull request classifier and one PR Gate, publish only from main, run broad checks on a schedule, and remove duplicate Fork CI and Security runs after merge. Include P21 routing and P22 security checks.
acceptance: Pass actionlint
Return exactly one required PR Gate result for every pull request path
Run only publication and smoke checks on main pushes, and run repeated broad checks on the schedule
nodes.falsification: Stop and repair PR Gate if a supported change can merge without a check that blocked it before, or if routing can leave a required result pending.

nodes.content: Check the delivery changes with workflow test data, matching local commands, Nix derivation comparisons, planted security test cases, and measured job estimates. Prove that code, documentation, dependency, and workflow-only pull requests all finish with the correct result.
acceptance: Run the intended jobs and final gate for every routing test case
Keep estimated post-merge documentation cost below 5 runner-minutes
Get an independent review with no security or publication regression
nodes.falsification: Return to P23 or P21 if a route skips a required check, leaves a required result pending, or rebuilds executable output for a documentation-only change.

nodes.content: Make RuntimePaths the single source for home, state, sessions, logs, cache, sockets, and test roots. Move normal tests to temporary roots, and allow access to the real ~/.jcode only in tests clearly marked as live.
acceptance: Create and remove temporary Jcode roots in normal tests
Read and write none of the operator's ~/.jcode in normal tests
Keep existing path behavior outside tests
nodes.falsification: Block completion if any normal test still requires the operator to stop running Jcode sessions.

nodes.content: Put executable lookup, repository and build metadata, running process identity, launch, termination, and reload state behind ReloadEnvironment. Remove mixed JCODE_TEST_SESSION branches from do_reload and keep strict failures for real sessions.
acceptance: Test reload behavior without discovering processes or repositories from the surrounding machine
Make stale daemon, newest binary, failed replacement, and recovery cases repeatable
Keep strict safety errors for real sessions
nodes.falsification: Narrow ReloadEnvironment before integration if it becomes a general service locator or hides production errors.

nodes.content: Use RuntimePaths and ReloadEnvironment throughout lifecycle and repeatability tests. Add a check that fails when a normal test touches the real ~/.jcode. Run the two-round lifecycle matrix while ordinary Jcode sessions remain active.
acceptance: Pass two lifecycle rounds in a row while normal Jcode sessions run
Leave no files in the real home or temporary roots
Provide source-backed evidence that issues #17 and #14 are fixed
nodes.falsification: Return to T20 or T21 after any interference from another session, race in the process-wide environment, or false reload match. Do not add sleeps or serialize the tests.

nodes.content: Independently test isolation and repeatable reload behavior during concurrent runs, crashes, restarts, and cleanup. Search testable production paths for hidden std::env changes and direct home-directory lookup.
acceptance: Pass isolation tests with live sessions and test processes running together
Leave no hidden write to the real home in normal tests
Get an independent review that approves closing the issues
nodes.falsification: Block architecture work after one repeatable test-to-test or live-session interference.

nodes.content: After the new commands and workflows are known, make a final list of reachable scripts and old files. Mark each deletion candidate as a supported command, current bug reproducer, benchmark, historical probe, or dead file.
acceptance: Check repository references and documented operator use for every candidate
Keep or move reproducers for open issues
Prepare a limited list of files to delete
nodes.falsification: Keep a file by default and ask a follow-up question when its operator owner is unknown.

nodes.content: After P23 creates the new pipeline, delete or move only files confirmed by C20. Remove old packaging, unsupported dispatch-only workflows, YAML-reading helpers, historical probes, and repeated scripts. Update every direct caller in the same commit.
acceptance: Remove at least 25 percent of script lines or explain every remaining exception
Keep every supported command and open-issue reproducer
Pass reference checks, shell syntax checks, and focused tests
nodes.falsification: Restore a deleted file and correct the list if a supported workflow, documented procedure, open issue, or operator command still uses it.

nodes.content: Stop required-check names and workflow documentation from drifting apart. Use scripts/required-checks.json or its replacement as the only list of named checks. Generate or link documentation from it, update stale workflow comments, and regenerate APM files.
acceptance: Use the same required check name in live rules, expected state, workflow jobs, and documentation
Pass APM validation and documentation reference checks
Keep no copied list of required checks in prose
nodes.falsification: Keep an automatic comparison if generated documentation can differ silently from the expected live state. Do not trust copied prose.

nodes.content: Check cleanup work and documentation. Run reference checks, confirm commands exist, run script syntax checks and tests, validate APM files, and compare repository size and file counts with the starting measurements.
acceptance: Make every documented command exist
Leave no active reference to a retired file
Measure the cleanup reduction and get an independent review
nodes.falsification: Return to C21 or C22 after any broken supported path or deletion without an explanation.

nodes.content: List the public APIs and imports that use the wildcard re-export chain. Prepare small automated edit batches, downstream compatibility tests, and starting compile times without changing production files.
acceptance: Map every wildcard export and every import that depends on it
Keep each migration batch small enough for a focused compile check
Record cold and warm compile times
nodes.falsification: Keep a layer that intentionally provides a stable API and has a measured compile benefit. Remove only its accidental exports.

nodes.content: Move repeated external dependencies into workspace.dependencies and adopt workspace = true in small steps. Keep all features and target-specific declarations, and choose one rand version deliberately.
acceptance: Pass Cargo metadata and machete
Change no dependency feature or target behavior by accident
Reduce repeated version declarations by a meaningful amount
nodes.falsification: Leave a dependency local if centralizing it hides different feature requirements or causes broad rebuilds that are not needed.

nodes.content: Remove the root crate wildcard re-export of jcode-tui. Change users to explicit crate and module paths, keep the intended root API small, and compare compile time and binary behavior with the A21 measurements.
acceptance: Remove the root wildcard re-export
Pass CLI, binary, example, and public API tests
Keep compile time within the agreed measurement noise
nodes.falsification: Stop this step and design a smaller API if it causes a meaningful compile or compatibility regression without clearer ownership.

nodes.content: Remove the jcode-tui wildcard re-export of jcode-app-core. Change the TUI and direct users to explicit imports, and keep presentation dependencies pointing in one direction.
acceptance: Remove the jcode-tui wildcard export of app-core
Make presentation crates import only declared APIs
Pass fast TUI tests and compile-time checks
nodes.falsification: Stop and repair the boundary if the change creates a dependency cycle or moves presentation details into app-core. Do not add another re-export.

nodes.content: Remove the jcode-app-core wildcard re-export of jcode-base. Use explicit imports and small APIs only where they are truly public. Then test provider, server, tool, session, and reload code.
acceptance: Remove the app-core wildcard export of base
Show layer ownership in Cargo metadata and imports
Pass workspace check, fast tests, and compile-time comparison
nodes.falsification: Redesign the API before continuing if the change only moves wildcard behavior or meaningfully increases the number of crates rebuilt by a change.

nodes.content: Reduce complexity in large production modules. Rank them by change frequency, number of dependents, error-handling debt, and compile cost. Expand this node into at most five separate child tasks. Each split needs a measured benefit, and no child may add a crate without proving a better boundary.
acceptance: Give each child separate files and a before-and-after complexity measurement
Add no production file longer than 1,200 lines
Improve at least three important modules without changing public behavior
nodes.falsification: Do not split a module when fewer lines do not improve ownership, testing, compile time, or the number of affected files.

nodes.content: Independently check the full architecture change. Compare dependency graphs, number of reverse dependencies, wildcard exports, compile times, public API behavior, and focused and full tests with the starting measurements.
acceptance: Remove the wildcard re-export chain or explain every API that remains
Meet the agreed compile and test limits
Get an independent review with no layer violation
nodes.falsification: Block B2 after any unexplained compatibility failure, dependency cycle, or compile-time slowdown.

nodes.content: Add a read-only CI metrics collector. Report pull request lead time, required-check delay, runner-minutes, cancellation, infrastructure failures, first-pass success, and release time in a workflow summary and saved artifact.
acceptance: Handle pagination, missing runs, and cancelled jobs
Commit no metrics to main
Show starting values and target SLOs in one summary
nodes.falsification: Use only public API data and temporary artifacts if the metrics need privileged secrets or would create commits.

nodes.content: Try cargo-nextest and scheduled llvm-cov without changing merge rules. Keep doctests and process-sensitive test groups explicit, produce slow-test and JUnit data, explain every ignored test, and keep nextest only if measurements show faster runs or better diagnostics.
acceptance: Keep doctests and process-sensitive test groups explicit
Give every ignored test a reason and runbook category
Keep nextest only after measuring a benefit
nodes.falsification: Remove nextest and keep only coverage and slow-test reports if it loses coverage, hides process-order bugs, or does not improve feedback.

nodes.content: Choose stable benchmarks for startup, warm compile time, TUI delay, and memory from existing tools. Use consistent machine-readable output, define nonblocking regression ranges, and remove repeated benchmark scripts found during cleanup.
acceptance: Repeat benchmarks reliably enough to set trend ranges
Keep output machine-readable and limited in size
Keep scheduled benchmark results nonblocking until their variation is understood
nodes.falsification: Keep a benchmark local and do not make it a noisy CI check if differences between hosts hide the signal.

nodes.content: Define the official fork release name and promotion process. Use v1.0.0 unless the operator chooses another name before tagging. Check main history, Cargo version, changelog, tag, cached Nix builds, SBOM, provenance, metadata-only GitHub Release, install, and rollback.
acceptance: Reject old v0 tags outside main history as release proof
Use or verify cached Nix output instead of adding a second binary channel
Keep rollback to the previous release documented and testable
nodes.falsification: Stop before publication and use one explicit fork-prefixed version name everywhere if v1.0.0 conflicts with a product decision.

nodes.content: Add O20 through O22 to the scheduled workflow and publish limited summaries and artifacts. Block pull requests only on stable checks that give repeatable results. Add no automatic retry that hides the first flaky failure.
acceptance: Pass scheduled workflow syntax checks and dry-run test data
Save metrics, coverage, and performance output without commits to main
Let no flaky retry hide a first failure
nodes.falsification: Reduce or split scheduled jobs before merge if they need unsupported credentials or exceed their time limit without useful output.

nodes.content: Check metrics and release readiness with test data, one local run equal to the scheduled workflow, a release rehearsal with a tag candidate that cannot publish, and an independent review of secrets, permissions, retention, and rollback.
acceptance: Report correct metrics for planted edge cases
Publish nothing during the release rehearsal and verify exact names and revisions
Keep workflow permissions at the minimum needed
nodes.falsification: Block B2 after any exposed secret, action reference that can change, wrong release name, or noisy metric that cannot guide action.

nodes.content: Combine the verified delivery, isolation, cleanup, architecture, metrics, and release work into one integration list. Confirm that every worker commit has limited scope, follows dependencies, and starts from the main branch that includes the governance update.
acceptance: Give every implementation node a limited commit and validation report
Resolve every low-confidence review
State the integration order and owner for each conflict
nodes.falsification: Block integration if work overlaps, uses an old base commit, or lacks verification.

nodes.content: Apply the commits approved by B2 to one fresh branch from the official main branch. Resolve conflicts without losing reviewed behavior, update only final documentation that crosses tasks, and record every Modernization-Node trailer.
acceptance: Include only approved node changes on the integration branch
Keep all tests and policy during conflict resolution
Record Modernization-Barrier: B2 and every node trailer
nodes.falsification: Stop and add one focused conflict-fix node if the reviewed commits cannot combine without redesign or lost behavior.

nodes.content: Run final local checks from narrow to broad: graph validation, APM validation, reference, security, and workflow checks, focused crate tests, the fast suite, preflight, Nix flake check, package and provenance build, and one clean install and startup test. Record real exit codes and leftover files.
acceptance: Pass every listed local and Nix check
Leave no files or processes in the real home, worktree, or build locations
Match measured command and package behavior to the design
nodes.falsification: Stop after a surprising or contradictory result. Check the assumption or test setup before running it again.

nodes.content: Independently try to find problems in the exact F30 commit. Repeat critical checks, inspect deletions and security boundaries, verify release names and rollback, and confirm that the work removed complexity instead of moving it.
acceptance: Name the exact commit and repeat critical checks independently
Resolve every high-severity finding
Measure changes in complexity and CI cost
nodes.falsification: Add a fix and another review node before publication for any high-severity problem in correctness, security, release, or recovery.

nodes.content: PERMISSION REQUIRED: after the user approves, push the reviewed integration branch and open the modernization pull request. Wait for PR Gate to pass. Then change the live rules from the old required checks to the reviewed PR Gate as one operation, confirm the pull request can merge, merge without bypass, and verify main. Restore the old rules if the merge cannot finish. Do not publish a release in this node.
acceptance: Pass the new PR Gate before changing live rules
Change the live rules in one operation to match the reviewed expected-state manifest
Merge without bypass and make the result reachable from the official main branch
nodes.falsification: Block the merge and restore the old rules after a PR Gate failure, missing result, rule change that is not atomic, merge failure, or live configuration mismatch.

nodes.content: Check the merged modernization from a fresh checkout and live GitHub state. Measure the first pull request and main workflow routes, confirm behavior for a documentation-only main change, test install and startup, and compare required checks with the expected-state manifest.
acceptance: Match live required checks and workflow layout to the target
Install from Cachix and start successfully in a fresh environment
Run no duplicate full suite after merge
nodes.falsification: Stop release work and fix main through a normal pull request if live behavior differs from the reviewed local behavior.

nodes.content: Schedule a read-only review for 30 days after publication. It must report pull request delay, runner-minutes, first-pass success, release time, test-isolation incidents, script-line reduction, and architecture measurements to the original session or a new audit session.
acceptance: Create a saved scheduled task with measurable success conditions
Make no external change without new user permission
Point the review to this graph and the published main commit
nodes.falsification: Create an issue milestone instead if the scheduler cannot deliver a reliable follow-up. Do not claim that an automatic review exists.

nodes.content: PERMISSION REQUIRED: after the user approves the final version and release notes, create the first official fork tag, run the release workflow, and create the metadata-only GitHub Release. Publish no binaries outside Nix.
acceptance: Point the tag to the official main branch and use the approved version name
Include install and rollback instructions in the release metadata
Verify Nix builds, the SBOM, and provenance
nodes.falsification: Block publication after any tag or version mismatch, missing cache output, provenance failure, or unexpected binary file.

nodes.content: Check the published release in a clean environment. Install and run the tagged Nix package, verify its version, provenance, and SBOM, reinstall the previous known-good revision, and confirm that the metadata-only release has no binary files.
acceptance: Install and start the tagged version
Complete rollback successfully
Make release metadata agree with the Nix-only policy
nodes.falsification: Keep the release node incomplete and use a normal repair pull request after a failed install, rollback, provenance check, or policy mismatch.

nodes.content: Write the final modernization result. Record before-and-after measurements, remaining limits, deferred work, exact published commits and tag, and the scheduled 30-day review. Stop owned swarm workers and leave no old task graph or worktree state.
acceptance: Record Modernization-Barrier: B3
Publish before-and-after measurements and clear remaining limits
Remove owned workers, branches, and worktrees after merge
nodes.falsification: Do not mark the work finished while any external check or scheduled follow-up is missing.
